onboardingIntro.message: Drowzy saves memory by putting inactive tabs to sleep. Your tabs are always safe – we use Chrome's native discard API, so they survive even if you uninstall Drowzy.

featureAutoSuspend.message: Tabs idle for 15 minutes are automatically suspended

featureZeroRam.message: Suspended tabs use zero RAM but stay in your tab bar

featureClickToWake.message: Click any suspended tab to instantly wake it up

featureProtected.message: Active, pinned, and audio tabs are never touched

actionClickIcon.message: Click the Drowzy icon in the toolbar to see all your tabs

actionAltS.message: Press <kbd>Alt+S</kbd> to suspend the current tab

actionAltShiftS.message: Press <kbd>Alt+Shift+S</kbd> to suspend all other tabs

actionAltW.message: Press <kbd>Alt+W</kbd> to wake all suspended tabs

actionRightClick.message: Right-click on any page for quick suspend options

onboardingCta.message: Drowzy is now running. Open it from your toolbar and hit "Suspend Others" to try it out.

privacyShortText.message: Drowzy doesn't collect any data. No analytics, no tracking, no external servers. Everything stays in your browser.

privacyStoredText.message: Your settings (suspend timer, whitelist, preferences) are saved using Chrome's built-in storage APIs: chrome.storage.sync for settings that follow your Chrome profile, chrome.storage.local for stats and saved sessions, and chrome.storage.session for temporary data like tab timestamps. None of this is sent to any third-party server.

privacyPermissionsIntro.message: Drowzy requests only the permissions it needs to do its one job:

privacyPermTabs.message: Listing, suspending, and restoring browser tabs.

privacyPermStorage.message: Saving your settings and sessions locally.

privacyPermAlarms.message: Periodic checks for inactive tabs (every 60 seconds).

privacyPermContextMenus.message: Right-click menu options for suspend and whitelist.

privacyPermScripting.message: Injecting a small script to detect unsaved form data before suspending a tab. Opt-in only.

privacyPermSidePanel.message: Displaying Drowzy in Chrome's side panel.

privacyPermHost.message: Optional host access, requested on-demand only when you enable Form Protection or Suspended-Tab Marking. Never requested at install. Revocable anytime.

privacyYourDataText.message: Because nothing leaves your browser, there's no dashboard, no account, and no way for us to see what you've done with Drowzy. If you uninstall Drowzy, Chrome offers you a chance to send optional feedback (reason for uninstalling, browser, OS) through a separate web page; that submission is explicit and goes to an anonymous form. You can skip it by closing the tab.

changelogCtaText.message: Drowzy is free and open source. If it's saving you memory, consider leaving a quick review or starring us on GitHub.

changelog136Title1.message: Every language is now fully translated

changelog136Desc1.message: A few strings (whitelist toasts, the Keyboard Shortcuts row, and the Share Stats text) were still showing in English in other languages. They are now translated across all 57 languages, and right-to-left languages like Arabic and Hebrew lay out correctly too.

changelog136Desc2.message: The "Enjoying Drowzy?" banner now appears only after you've used Drowzy for a while, never on install or right after an update. The buttons are Leave a review, Maybe later, and Don't ask again. It never asks for a specific star rating and never offers a reward.

changelog135Desc1.message: The default timer is now 15 minutes so you notice the memory savings sooner, and suspending other tabs and closing duplicates are more reliable.

changelog135Desc2.message: Clearer remove buttons, confirmation messages, and a site count, plus it now works for localhost and IP addresses.

changelog135Desc3.message: A new Settings row shows your shortcut status and links straight to where you can customize them.

changelog135Desc4.message: Share Stats now appears in your language, and memory totals read cleanly, for example 2 GB instead of 2.0 GB.

changelog135Desc5.message: Clearer icons, a brand-matched toolbar badge, better screen-reader labels, and a tidier popup.

suspendThisTabHint.message: Switch away and put this tab to sleep

changelog137Title1.message: Put a single tab back to sleep

changelog137Desc1.message: After you wake a sleeping tab to look at it, the new Suspend this tab button in the popup and side panel sends just that tab back to sleep. It switches you to another tab first, because the tab you're viewing can't be suspended.
